title: ACA s. 11 — Appointment of arbitrators (ACA s. 11)

content.overview: Section 11 regulates appointment of arbitrators where the parties' agreed appointment procedure fails or the statutory intervention mechanism is triggered. It preserves party autonomy while providing a judicial/designated-authority route for constituting the tribunal.
content.glance: Section 11 regulates appointment of arbitrators where the parties' agreed appointment procedure fails or the statutory intervention mechanism is triggered. It preserves party autonomy while providing a judicial/designated-authority route for constituting the tribunal.
content.study:
Section 11 — Appointment of arbitrators

The parties are free to agree on a procedure for appointing the arbitrator or arbitrators. Where that procedure fails, section 11 supplies the statutory mechanism for appointment through the designated judicial authority in the circumstances specified by the Act.

The section must be read with section 10 on tribunal size and section 12 on disclosures, qualifications and independence. The precise appointment route depends on the number of arbitrators and the agreed procedure. The central drafting enquiry is therefore whether the agreed procedure has been followed and, if not, what statutory appointment mechanism applies.

examples.title: Application 1
examples.body: The parties agree on three arbitrators and each party appoints one in accordance with the clause; the two appointees must then constitute the tribunal in accordance with the agreed/statutory procedure.

examples.title: Application 2
examples.body: An agreed appointment step fails; counsel must identify the precise default and invoke the corresponding section 11 mechanism rather than inventing a different appointment route.
